Heard Sri K. Anandkumar, learned counsel for appellant and Sri RP Rajnal, learned counsel for respondent no.3-Insuer.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 09.07.2012 passed by Fast Track Court III & Additional MACT, Belgavi1 in MVC no.1851/2009, this appeal is filed.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for appellant submitted that on 05.08.2007 when claimant a vegetable vendor was riding his bicycle by side of road, driver of a Tempo Trax bearing registration no.KA-23/M-1834 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against cycle causing accident.
Claimant sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to hospital.
Despite treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, he filed claim petition against owner and insurer of Tempo Trax.
For short, 'Tribunal' NC: 2026:KHC-D:3545 HC-KAR 4.
Respondent no.2 did not appear despite service of notice and was placed exparte.
Respondent no.1 though appeared did not file objections.
Only respondent no.3-Insurer filed objections opposing claim petition on all counts.

sentences.text: Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW1 and Dr.S.D. Patil as PW2 and got marked documents at Exs.P1 P13.

Respondent examined its official as RW1 and got marked documents at Exs.R1 to R6.
6.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tempo Trax by its driver, vehicle was insured with respondent no.3-Insurer and claimant was entitled for compensation as follows from Insurer:
 Injury, Pain and Agony 30,000/-
 Minimum medical Expenses 40,000/-
 Nursing, Attendant Charges Extra 5,000/-
 Nourishment & Conveyance  Loss of earning during treatment 5,000/-
 Loss of future earning 77,000/-
 Loss of amenities & future unhappiness 12,000/-
 Total 1,69,000/-
7.
Dissatisfied with quantum of compensation, claimant was in appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3545 HC-KAR 8.
It was firstly submitted, claimant had stated that he was 27 years old, working as vegetable vendor and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
However, without any justification, Tribunal considered Rs.3,750/- as monthly income and awarded inadequate compensation.
It was submitted, claimant had sustained communited fracture of middle 1/3 right tibia and fibula, assessed by PW2 to have caused 33% disability to affected limb as per Ex.P8-disability certificate.
However, Tribunal considered loss of earning capacity at only 10% and awarded inadequate compensation.

9. Apart from above, it was submitted, even compensation awarded towards pain and suffering, loss of income during laid up period and incidental expenses as well as towards loss of amenities, was on lower side and sought enhancement.
10. On other hand, learned counsel for respondent no.3- Insurer opposed appeal.

11. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused impugned judgment and award.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3545 HC-KAR 12.

From above and since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?"

sentences.text: 13. Though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.6,000/- per month as a vegetable vendor, same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, Tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.
But notional income for year 2007 being Rs.4,000/-, Tribunal was not justified in assessing it at Rs.3,750/-.
Indeed PW2-Dr.S.D. Patil, on examination of claimant assessed limb disability at 33% and issued disability certificate marked at Ex.P8.

Perusal of said certificate as well as deposition of PW2, would reveal that claimant had sustained restriction of movement of right knee by 30 degrees and right ankle by 15 degrees, making it difficult if not impossible to squat and sit for long duration.

Since vegetable vending would require claimant to sit while selling vegetables,
disability would affect earning capacity.
14. Under such circumstances, consideration of 10% disability by Tribunal would appear inadequate and is enhanced NC: 2026:KHC-D:3545 HC-KAR to 15%.
Claimant was 27 years of age, multiplier applicable would be 17.

Thus, loss of future income would be as follows:
4,000x12x15%x17 = Rs.1,22,400/-
15.
Claimant sustained fracture of right tibia and fibula, i.e., to a structural bone.

Therefore,
claimant would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering instead of Rs.30,000/-
awarded by Tribunal.
16. Since, there is complete reimbursement of amount for which bills were produced, award of compensation towards medical expenses at Rs.40,000/- is confirmed.

17. Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards Nursing, Attendant Charges, Extra Nourishment &
Conveyance.
Considering inpatient period of treatment of 16 days, same would appear grossly inadequate and stands enhanced to Rs.16,000/-.
Normally fractures take about 3 months to heal.
Considering said period as a layoff, claimant would be entitled for Rs.12,000/- towards loss of earning during treatment.
18. When claimant has sustained permanent physical disability, award of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of amenities by Tribunal would be inadequate.
Same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3545 HC-KAR 19.
Deposition of PW2 would indicate that insertion of rod at fracture side.
Claimant would require to undergo surgery for its removal.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled for Rs.25,000/- towards same.

20. Thus, claimant is held entitled for total reassessed compensation as follows:
 Injury, Pain and Agony 40,000/-
 Minimum medical Expenses 40,000/-
 Nursing, Attendant Charges Extra 16,000/-
 Nourishment & Conveyance  Loss of earning during treatment 12,000/-

Consequently, following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed, judgment and award dated 09.07.2012 passed by Fast Track Court III & Additional MACT, Belagavi in MVC no.1851/2009, is modified and claimant held is entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.2,85,400/- as against Rs.1,69,000/-.

(iv) On deposit, Tribunal is directed to release it in favour of claimant.
